safety.r1_summary:
Safety fixer done. All work is server-side in lib/lrg_dialogue.php (tagged [pt19h-safety]), plus a 113-check [pt19h-safety] section in tools/test_dialogue.php. Nothing was deployed and no floor was lowered. Report: research/pt19h-safety.md.

The main change: S4.5's $hit exemption now holds only for the line's own words. When his sentence contains the whole line, a new function (lrgDlgQuoteQualm) judges the words around it: "not now, <line> later", "no, <line>", "wait, <line>?", "is it true that <line>", "<line>? says who". The same step-0 test (refusal, deferral, hedge, question around the line) now runs before every lrgDlgExplicit return, including the enlistment branch. Other changes:
- The engine's own Yes/No layer no longer releases her key after his refusal or question.
- LEAVE (and the leave guard) takes only a real back-out line: unscripted, not a commit, and a back-out phrase leads one of its sentences.
- Negation parity handles double negatives, "no sense" and "almost / nearly".
- Tag questions and "haven't you" count as questions.
- Protected lines need the same question (lrgDlgQuestionsSame).
- A statement never picks a question line (lrgDlgDeclares); a request must fit the line (lrgDlgRequestFits); a swapped opposite or name is a near-miss (lrgDlgSubstitutes).
- Generic display names are no longer names.

- say lines clicked on the fast path: 58.7% to 61.7%; about 33 say lines now go to her key or one question because of my rules, none to a wrong click.

So 'do you have any more contracts' (Nazir, DB02a set3/set5 commit and set4 scripted; a recurring ask) and 'do you have another contract for me?' lost the fast path. 'are there any more contracts' still clicks. Fix: only know / remember / have any idea is the knowledge sense; 'do you have' and 'got any' mean the same as 'is there'.

- A line whose only question follows a lead clause loses its words-park: 'who are you?' / 'Forget me, who are you?'. Fix: compare against the line's last question clause.

- The line said verbatim must never be refused. Fix: strip the same vocative from the line before comparing (lrgDlgBareWords on the line text with the same npc), or accept at once when his raw words equal the line. It is rare in the index (about 20 name-led question lines), but it is a correctness bug.

The new refusals are in lrgDlgSingleEntryRelease; the re-arm is lrgDlgRearmLine, the S4.6 auto-advance eligibility the fixer owns, and it was left unchanged. [arch] P3: the S4.4 park release (lrgDlgParkOrRelease, not the own-confirmation branch, and lrgDlgBareYesLine through it) still releases a parked COMMIT on phrasings the new rules refuse everywhere else. Trace C2/C2b, 'I'm ready to join the Legion.' parked after her naming question. Limit the 'restates' exemption to lines where lrgDlgEntryIsQuestion is true. [lang] P1 (FAILS a first-evening gate; safety's code). lrgDlgWordsQualm now calls lrgDlgDeclares before the S4.5 single release on the words path. So a leading assent plus a statement, said to a commit single that is a question, is refused. Example: "yes, I'll help", "sure, I'll help" and "of course I'll help" on Balgruuf's single "What else can I help you with?" now give nothing (the baseline released them). This is the spec's own S4.5 step-1 example. `php tools/test_questline.php --first-evening --words` FAILS 2 rows (F.balgruuf.reward, W.balgruuf.reward.never), and `--words` has 8 lines worse than its baseline. The fixer never ran `--words`. The fast path and the key path still release. Fix: skip Declares and the question tests in WordsQualm when the entry is the layer's single (let lrgDlgSingleEntryRelease decide, as the code comment already says), or exempt a leading assent (confirm.assent_words) in lrgDlgDeclares.

[lang] P2 (STT variants lose their explicit line). lrgDlgExplicit has a new test: a question with a word of its own is not the line. Its $slip closure checks only stem, levenshtein up to a third of the letters, or raw metaphone, and only against the line's STRICT words. It ignores the line's stop-word tokens, the codebase's own STT echo test (lrgDlgSoundsLike / lrgDlgOwnWords), dropped apostrophes and expanded contractions or auxiliaries. So the verbatim question with one STT slip now parks on a commit, where the baseline was explicit. Examples: "whos the target" (Who's the target?), "where would a moss priest go", "do you think this wood help", "so why haven't you arrested hem", "can you help me find the stuff of magnus or knot", "do you know where these udder scrolls are", "what's so important about these climbs", "did something go long", "where did he goal", "do you still wanna come with me", "would you grant entry to the drag and born", "what could a dog need help whiff". Plain rewordings fail the same way: "I am looking for Miraak. Do you know him?" (am), "will you help me escape" / "will you help me find the staff or not" (will), "what did you expect from the listener" (did). In the measurer's r12 output against the baseline, this one test takes 29 extended say lines off the fast path, 14 of them STT. Fix: take his own words from lrgDlgOwnWords($bare,$e) minus the frame list. Add the auxiliaries am/is/are/was/were/will/would/did/do/does/can/could/shall/should/may/might/has/have/had and wanna/gonna/gotta to the question frame. Fold apostrophes.

[lang] P3 (lrgDlgDeclares is too broad, on every path). It reads a yes/no question whose `?` the STT dropped, and a request in statement form, as a statement against a question line. All of these clicked on the baseline and now miss the fast path. Alvor's "Do you have any supplies I could take?": "you got any supplies i could take with me" and "you got any supplies". Nazir: "you got any more contracts for me". J'zargo's "What did you need help with?": "you needed help with something" and "you need help with something". Alvor's "How do I get to Whiterun from here?": "I need to get to Whiterun". "Is there any work to be done?": "I'm here for work". Brynjolf's "I'm sorry, what?": the STT stutter "i'm sorry what what". Aventus: "you ok" and "you okay kid". The adversarial STT row "you got any supplies i could take with me" went from resolve to nothing in --words. Fix: a 'you' sentence carrying any/anything/anyone/ever/still (a declarative yes/no question) against a yn:you line is his question with its `?` lost. "I need / I want / I'm here for / I'm after X" against a line that asks for X (do you have any X, is there any X, how do I get to X) is a request, not an answer. Let the one-word-difference rule tolerate a repeated token.

[lang] P4 (lrgDlgQuestionsSame is too strict for natural paraphrase pairs). (a) The is-THERE / do-YOU split also catches possession: "do you have any more contracts" against "Are there any more contracts available?" (DB02a set3, set4, set5) and "have you got work for me" against "Is there any work to be done?". Keep the split only for a yn:you question about her knowledge (know, think, remember, seen, heard), not have/got. (b) how/what and where/how: "how do I get into Riftweald Manor" / "how can I get into Riftweald Manor?" against "What's the best way to get into Riftweald Manor?", and "where can I find your master" against "How can I find your master?", no longer resolve. (c) A VERBATIM line lost the fast path: "Kodlak, is that you?" on C06.kodlak.isthatyou (scripted). lrgDlgBareWords strips 'Kodlak' from his words, lrgDlgQuestionKind reads the vocative-led entry as an echo, and the echo coverage then requires 'kodlak'. "is that you, Kodlak" fails too. Fix: skip a leading vocative in the entry's QuestionKind, and do not count the stripped vocative as missing coverage. (d) The echo branch skips the G2 compound fold: "alright?" and "everything alright?" against Aventus's "Are you all right?" (DB01 first contact) went from fast pick to none.

[lang] P5 (lrgDlgQuoteQualm reads a follow-up question as an echo). $moreQ counts every `?` after the point where the line starts. So "<line>, <new question>?" counts as the line asked back. "Speaking of which, my payment?" and "speaking of which, uh, where's my pay?" on TG02's scripted single "Speaking of which..." now give nothing on the fast, key and words paths. Combined with the existing dispute rule, there is also no auto-advance, so the beat stalls. The baseline released it, and the same sentence without the `?` still releases. "I'm looking to apply to the college, is there a way in?" / "..., how do I get in?" now give nothing on key and words (the enlistment path still saves the fast path). Fix: count his `?` as asking the line only when it closes the line's own clause (the `?` directly after the line's last token, or after an echo frame), never a later clause of his.

[lang] P6 (a false deferral after the quoted line). QuoteQualm's $defer list includes 'first' (and 'soon'), taken anywhere after the line. "I'm ready to learn about my new powers, show me the first one" and "I'm ready to learn about my new powers first" on Harkon's commit now park; the baseline was explicit. After the line, 'first' puts the line first, and in "the first one" it is an ordinal. Fix: take 'first' only as "but first ..." / "first I ...", or at the end of a clause other than the line's.

[lang] P7 (unanchored refusal phrases drop parks; this contradicts pt19c-language R1/R2). The new lrgDlgIsBackOut pattern `(we|i|you)('d| had)? better not|not today|not this time|some other time|go away|leave me alone|get lost` matches ANYWHERE. So an assent is read as a refusal, and a parked commit is UNPARKED where the baseline kept it and asked again. Examples: "yes, we'd better not keep them waiting", "yes, I'd better not waste any time", "yes, and you better not cheat me", "yes, and don't get lost on the way", "yes, I'll do it, leave me alone about it", "yes, go away and let me work". "let's go, we'd better not keep Mercer waiting" is a step-0 refusal on Karliah's commit single "Let's go.". Fix: anchor these phrases the way R1 anchors not/no/never: leading (after up to 2 fillers) or the whole reply.

[lang] P8 (the hedge rule gives different answers on different paths). "I guess that's where I come in", "I suppose that's where I come in" and "I guess so" release Viarmo's scripted single "And that's where I come in?" on the FAST and KEY paths (S4.5 step 2). The WORDS path refuses the same sentences as a hedge on a protected line. "and that's where I come in, I guess" is now refused on all paths. The adversarial row "I suppose that's where I come in" went from resolve to nothing in --words, although lrgDlgDeclares' own comment accepts that sentence. "I guess / I suppose" + a fact (that's / it's / you're ...) is an inference, not a hedged commitment. Fix: lrgDlgHedges should take i guess / i suppose only before his own commitment (I'll, I will, I can, we should, so, or bare), and all three paths should apply the same rule.

[lang] P9 (the 40% fragment rule counts an assent particle as content). "I'll do it" against "Fine, I'll do it." (DBDestroy.maro.accept, commit) is no longer explicit: the line's strict words are [fine], so coverage is 0, although he said the whole commitment. Fix: remove the assent or interjection lead of the line (confirm.assent_words: fine, very well, alright, agreed, yes...) from its strict words before the fragment test. Related: "I want to join the Legion" on Tullius's line now parks on the key path (3 of 8 strict words), though the enlistment fast path still clicks.

[lang] P10 (minor: the almost/nearly scope in the negation-parity change). "I almost gave up but I found your crystal" (no comma before 'but') clashes on 'found'. The commit key now returns nothing, not even a park; the baseline was explicit. "I barely killed them both" is read as negated, but barely/hardly + an achievement verb asserts the predicate ("I barely made it out" = I made it). Fix: limit almost/nearly to the next verb, treat 'but' as a clause stop, and take barely/hardly/scarcely as negators only before know / any / ever / stative predicates.
